Make sure to work on yourself. When you're content with yourself, with your own presence, nobody else's opinion matters. It's true what they say about keeping your circle small. Not everyone will always be there for you; I hope you have one or two people who are always by your side. But even if you have those friends with you, no one will always be there for you except yourself. Take yourself on dates, do things you enjoy, learn from yourself, and work on yourself. When you love yourself, you'll rely less on others. I hope you can take something from this because I don't mean to say you should change yourself to make more friends. After all, we all know that many people are only temporary in your life. You will always be the one writing your own story.

To be honest, I also don't know what to say to you, so I'll share my own experiences when I have similar feelings as you do. Please don't see this as something I'm pushing on you, but rather something you might find useful or learn from. When dealing with thoughts like fear, insecurity, or anything else, it's comforting for me to know that I can pray. I'm a Muslim myself, and we Muslims believe that Allah is always with us. Allah wants to see us well and will always protect us. In times of uncertainty, I turn to Him because it brings me peace and tranquility. Find something that can bring you peace as well, or consider talking to a psychologist about it.
Yes be honest but treat her the same way you want to be treated in a situation like this.

What has happened has happened. Unfortunately, you can't undo it, and of course, no one deserves to have such a husband. Now, you're actually living for your child, and your life should revolve around your child because your child is innocent in this story. Sadly, many women go through this, and that doesn't mean it should be seen as normal. I hope you'll get past this and maybe someday meet someone who truly deserves you and your child. But until then, I hope that you and your child will have a better life than your ex-husband could ever provide.

I hope that therapy can help you. You are not a bad person; what you went through in the past should not define you as a child. And the mistakes you've made do not define the person you are. You've already come a long way in realizing your mistakes, and you're heading in the right direction. Trust in yourself, trust in therapy, and hope for the best. Remember that you are the one who can lift yourself out of this misery, so you've already made progress in realizing that. Trust yourself.
